messages:
maria: Heads up — several staging deploys started failing after last night's token rotation. app logs show 403 on Redwood API calls. Anyone else seeing this?

devon: Can you paste the error snippet and which service account?

maria: paste from deploy log:
```
ERROR 2024-06-12T03:12:08Z deployer: request failed: 403 Forbidden
body: {"error":"permission_denied", "message":"token expired or insufficient scope"}
headers: X-Redwood-Auth-Error: token_scope_mismatch
```
Service account: ci-deployer@redwood-sa (bot)

sam-k: That header is interesting — looks like an auth-exchange or scope mismatch rather than pure expiry. Any chance the runner caches tokens between jobs?

ashley: ci-deployer was provisioned via SCIM and the SA token TTL policy was 7d, but our infra rotation script rotated credentials nightly and we also recently tightened the impersonation window in IAM. Could be a mismatch.

maria: Reproduced locally on a long-running job (10+ min): first few stages succeed then calls start 403'ing. Decoded JWT from the runner at failure time shows exp is in the past. Decoded payload snippet:
```
{
  "sub": "serviceAccount:ci-deployer@redwood-sa",
  "aud": "redwood-ci",
  "exp": 1718199500
}
```

devon: OK that proves expiry. Two likely roots: 1) runner process cached token and never refreshed, 2) token exchange service returned a token with too-short TTL for long jobs. Which CI image are you using?

maria: Using our shared kubernetes-runner image: redwood/ci-runner:stable-2024-06. We call the metadata endpoint once at job start and export REDWOOD_TOKEN to env.

ops-bot: automation.log: "token-exchange: job=staging-deploy id=1234 refresh_needed=false token_exp=1718199500 now=1718200208"

sam-k: That log shows the refresh window check is inverted — token_exp < now but refresh_needed=false. Looks like the runner's clock skew + race on rotation. We also recently enabled token caching for speed.

ashley: Short-term mitigation: restart the runner pod to flush env and force fresh token, or open pipeline and add a pre-step to call the exchange endpoint before the deploy stage.

maria: Restarted one runner pod, re-ran the job — deploy completed successfully. :white_check_mark:

devon: For a cleaner fix: update the runner image to refresh tokens when remaining_ttl < 300s and add retries on exchange failure. Example pseudo-step:
```
# pseudo
TOK=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://metadata.internal/v1/impersonate?sa=ci-deployer")
EXP=$(jwt_decode_exp $TOK)
if [ $((EXP - $(date +%s))) -lt 300 ]; then
  TOK=$(curl -sS -X POST "https://metadata.internal/v1/impersonate?sa=ci-deployer&force=true")
fi
export REDWOOD_TOKEN=$TOK
```
Also ensure the audience is validated: audience must be "redwood-ci" for pipeline tokens.

ashley: We'll also tighten IAM so the SA only has minimal scopes: ["inference.generate","embeddings.create"] and restrict the policy to the staging project. That prevents broader exposure if a token is leaked.

maria: Filing a support ticket and infra PR. Ticket: SUP-8392 — includes logs, runner image tag, and reproduction steps. Assigning to @devon and @sam-k.

devon: Long-term: add jittered background refresher in runner, log when token refresh fails, and an alert if >1% of jobs see 403 auth errors in a 10m window.

sam-k: I'll open a patch for the runner and add a smoke check in our preflight that verifies token_exp > job_duration_estimate + 60s.

maria: Thanks all. Workaround worked for now, keeping ticket open until runner image is patched.

ops-bot: support ticket SUP-8392 created and linked to infra queue.
